lines: -The death-avoidance finding in ScienceWorld raises a natural question: does routing signal persist in environments without catastrophic failure? An evaluation on MATH Level~4--5 (300 problems: 152 Level~4, 148 Level~5), using code interpreter as the deterministic modality, suggests not. Internal reasoning directionally outperforms code interpreter: 81.0\% accuracy (95\% CI [76.7, 85.3]) versus 76.7\% (95\% CI [72.0, 81.3]); the paired difference of $+4.3$~percentage points (95\% CI [0.0, $+8.7$]; McNemar $p = 0.079$) shows a directional reversal, though not statistically significant at the 95\% level. The label distribution inverts relative to ScienceWorld: 30 internal-preferred versus 17 deterministic-preferred (compared to 9:86 in ScienceWorld), with 84.3\% of problems (253 of 300) showing no modality preference. In the absence of death risk, the routing signal vanishes or reverses---consistent with death avoidance as the primary driver of the deterministic strategy's advantage observed in ScienceWorld. Figure~\ref{fig:signal-reversal} visualizes this label distribution inversion.

+The death-avoidance finding in ScienceWorld raises a natural question: does routing signal persist in environments without catastrophic failure? The label distribution inverts relative to ScienceWorld: 30 internal-preferred versus 17 deterministic-preferred (compared to 9:86 in ScienceWorld), with 84.3\% of problems (253 of 300) showing no modality preference. In the absence of death risk, the routing signal vanishes or reverses---consistent with death avoidance as the primary driver of the deterministic strategy's advantage observed in ScienceWorld. Figure~\ref{fig:signal-reversal} and Table~\ref{tab:cross-env} summarize this label distribution inversion.
